judgments.reason: The study paper reports the AMUSE auditory spelling online study with N=21 subjects, matching the dataset's 21 subjects, AMUSE paradigm, and authors Schreuder and Tangermann.
judgments.paper_title: Listen, You are Writing! Speeding up Online Spelling with a Dynamic Auditory BCI

judgments.reason: The 2010 PLoS ONE paper reports an offline oddball study with 10 subjects; this dataset has 21 subjects and is anchored to the 2011 Frontiers paper, so it is earlier related work by the same group.
judgments.paper_title: A New Auditory Multi-Class Brain-Computer Interface Paradigm: Spatial Hearing as an Informative Cue

judgments.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiological data into BIDS, used in curating the dataset, not a paper describing the AMUSE dataset.
judgments.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
judgments.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software

judgments.reason: EEG-BIDS is a specification/standard extension for organizing EEG data, used to format this dataset, not a paper describing the AMUSE auditory ERP data.
judgments.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
